content:
A former fervent Trump supporter has broken ranks with the president, saying her trust in him began to crumble when he reacted aggressively to a "reasonable question" from a reporter about Jeffrey Epstein.

Trisha Hope joined "Front Row Joes," a group of supporters who follow Trump to events, in 2018. She pointed to a heated moment during a July 2025 Cabinet meeting, when Trump cut off then-Attorney General Pam Bondi after she was asked about the Justice Department's files on the deceased sex offender.

Trump said at the time: "Are you still talking about Jeffrey Epstein? This guy has been talked about for years."

Hope told Politico's Dasha Burns the president's words "felt like a dagger in my heart."

Hope, who published a book compiling Trump's posts on X, formerly Twitter, during his first term, said: "It was like a light switch just came on, the veil was lifted from my eyes, and I saw him for who he is, and I could never unsee it."

Hope, who once spent weeks meeting with lawmakers at the US Capitol to defend Trump during his first impeachment, has since turned against him.

She also pointed to Trump's having told Americans "up to 600 times" that the war he launched against Iran was over as another source of her disillusionment.

Of that conflict, she said: "He told us Iran has no army, has no navy, but they're still blowing things up. It's all lies. You can't believe anything he says. It's terrifying..." according to a recent poll that found 70% of Americans believed the conflict had "harmed" the country.

She added: "The message I want to get across is if we do lose the midterms, if he is impeached again, I will be walking those Capitol hallways supporting that impeachment."

Hope told Burns she had invested "so much" in the MAGA movement and believed Trump was America's "last hope."

She added: "I believed what he said, I believed he actually cared about America, but he doesn't, he only cares about himself."
